one_sentence_story: Your brain stores a person's face and facts in one room, and the sound of their name in a next room. Straining for thirty seconds trains that stuck door to jam again.
so_what_for_you: Do not panic when names freeze past age 40, and do not grind for a full minute. Look the name up fast and say it out loud once to fix the link.

jargon_map.plain: you know the full meaning of a word, but the wire to its sound is weak
jargon_map.analogy: like seeing a song title on screen when the speaker wire is loose

jargon_map.plain: a wrong name with the same first sound that keeps popping up in the way
jargon_map.analogy: like pulling into the wrong driveway right next door

jargon_map.plain: stewing in a word block teaches your brain to repeat that same stall later
jargon_map.analogy: like spinning car tires in mud until the rut gets deeper

jargon_map.plain: names have just one link to their sound, while common nouns have many
jargon_map.analogy: like an island with one narrow footbridge instead of five roads
